- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

Add `--hca-aligned-backward` (default off) using NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1198. Supports GB300/Rubin, contiguous CP4/8/16, and 8K–128K tokens with 128-token-aligned local chunks. Requires BF16, H128/D512, window/compression 128, and one padded sequence per pack. Other eager layouts use stock backward; cuDNN's capability query controls eligibility.

Preserves existing forward, output RoPE and KV reconstruction. CUDA graph replay requires fixed pack boundaries and eager backward warmup. The configuration comment reflects the broader support.

Validation: Hecate/Rubin job **637018** passed 66 MCore and 55 frontend tests, 56 shape/rank cases, and three memchecks. Saved 15-layer, 30-step comparisons: **637939**, 32K/CP8, **0.23%** step-time reduction; **637940**, 64K/CP16, **1.78%**. All ten arms were finite; loss/gradient-norm agreement passed. The generalized 64K result remained near parity with the previous implementation. CP4 and other sequence lengths have attention-level coverage; earlier GB300 validation is recorded in job **3144587**.

Review follow-ups: prepare eager packing once per microbatch, skip no-grad HCA selection, require explicit CP size, and drop unused saved index metadata. Backend checks precede capture guards. Reconciled with current `dev`.

Latest validation (Hecate/Rubin): **894182**, **136 correctness + 332 determinism/registry checks passed**; **894212**, bit-exact outputs/gradients and attention backward within **0.3%** of the previous PR at 32K/CP8 and 64K/CP16.

## Strict review: opt-in aligned HCA backward (#7625)

**Findings:** CRITICAL 0, IMPORTANT 1, SUGGESTION 3. **Overall risk: low.**

The flag is off by default and eligibility is checked conservatively. With the flag off, or on an ineligible layout, the stock backward runs unchanged. I found no correctness defect that could produce wrong gradients.

### Most important finding
- **[IMPORTANT Performance]** ([csa.py L3993](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L3993)): HCA selection also runs in forward passes that never reach backward.
  - Setup: Transformer Engine (TE) CUDA graphs that capture attention. In that setup [`prepare_packed_seq_params`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/training/utils/packed_seq_utils.py#L32) skips the per-microbatch preparation. Evaluation then runs eagerly, because TE graphs require `self.training` ([module.py L812-L822](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/module.py#L812-L822)).
  - Result: every HCA layer falls back to the live `.item()` in [`_is_single_sequence`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/aligned_hca.py#L61). That is the per-layer sync the review follow-up removed from eager training, and the result is never used because backward does not run.
  - Fix: one line — select only when `torch.is_grad_enabled()`.

### Suggestions
- **`hca_cp_size` defaults to 16.** This appears in three signatures, and the parameter is missing from the docstring. A future caller that passes only `hca_cp_rank` would silently get the CP16 layout ([fused_sparse_attention.py L2026](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L2026)).
- **`topk_idxs` is still saved for backward when the HCA backward is used**, even though that backward never reads it ([fused_sparse_attention.py L1953](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L1953)).
- **The new determinism-manifest note is incomplete.** It doesn't name the external kernel or explain how determinism is achieved. It also doesn't say that its replay test skips on the H100 kernel bucket ([manifest.py L135](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py#L135)).

### Checked, no issues found
- **Selection rule vs. the real `_forward_thd_cp` key/value (KV) layout.**
  - For ratio 128, the compressor capacity per rank is `c_cap = (l_local + 128) // 128` with alignment 1 ([thd_layout_kernels.py L1123-L1126](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/thd_layout_kernels.py#L1123-L1126)). With 128-aligned chunks that equals `l_local // 128 + 1`, so the `kv` shape check matches `cat(boundary, local, rank-major compressed)`.
  - The path without an indexer builds its attention indices from the padded `cu_seqlens` (`cu_seqlens_unpadded=None`). That matches the single-padded-sequence rule HCA assumes.
  - Window-only layers, indexer layers and the indexer-loss path never reach the HCA call.
- **Autograd.**
  - There are 13 forward inputs and 13 gradients are returned.
  - The new parameters come last and have defaults, so existing positional callers are unaffected.
  - When `kv` is rebuilt from its saved parts for backward, and when output RoPE is undone, the HCA branch sees the same tensors as the stock branch.
- **Prepared-verdict safety.**
  - The cached verdict is keyed on the `cu` tensor's identity, `cu._version` and the sequence length, and it is refreshed every microbatch.
  - `finalize_packed_seq_params` mutates the object in place.
  - `max_seqlen_q` is a Python `int` in the training pipelines, so the `!=` comparison stays on the host.
  - Moving the `cuda_graph_captures_attention` import to module level adds no import cycle: `transformer_config` already imports `cuda_graph_config`.
  - Configs without the flag short-circuit, so behaviour is unchanged.
- **Earlier reviewer feedback ([ghadiaravi13](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7625), comments on an older commit).** Both points are addressed in the current code:
  - `supports_configuration` now runs before the capture-time `_assert_async` ([aligned_hca.py L106-L115](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/aligned_hca.py#L106-L115)).
  - The per-layer `.item()` is replaced by the per-microbatch prepared verdict in eager training. The finding above covers the remaining eval path.
- **Config, CLI, tests.**
  - `--hca-aligned-backward` is generated automatically from `TransformerConfig`.
  - The hybrid-MoE config snapshot is updated.
  - `kind="dispatch"` is a valid manifest kind, and the registered source changes together with its replay test.
  - Each fallback-test case trips the check it targets.
- **Fatal device assert under graph replay when pack boundaries change.** This is documented in the config docstring ("Captured replay must preserve boundaries"), and because the backend choice is fixed when the graph is captured, there is no safe fallback during replay. I treat it as an intentional design choice.

### Limitations
- I could not inspect the external cuDNN Frontend `AlignedHCABackward` / `aligned_hca_backward_wrapper` (NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1198). Its numerics and the determinism claim rest on the PR's GPU parity and replay tests, which I did not run.
- I split the review into three areas and gave each to a delegated reviewer. The report for the dispatch/autograd area never reached me, so I inspected that area myself; the conclusions above are my own.

**[IMPORTANT Performance]** HCA selection also runs in forward passes that can never reach backward. In the TE-graph eval path this adds back one device→host sync per HCA layer.

**How it happens**
- **Setup:** `hca_aligned_backward=True`, `cuda_graph_impl="transformer_engine"`, `cuda_graph_modules` empty or containing `attn`, an eligible layout, and periodic evaluation (`model.eval()` under `torch.no_grad()`).
- **No preparation:** [`prepare_packed_seq_params`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/training/utils/packed_seq_utils.py#L32) skips the HCA preparation whenever `cuda_graph_captures_attention(config)` is true, so `_aligned_hca_sequence` is never set.
- **Eval runs eagerly:** TE graphs require `self.training` ([module.py L812-L822](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/module.py#L812-L822)), so this branch runs outside the graph.
- **Per-layer sync:** `aligned_hca_cp_rank` → [`_is_single_sequence`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/aligned_hca.py#L61) has no prepared verdict, so it calls `.item()` on the CUDA `cu_seqlens`. That is one device→host sync per HCA layer per eval microbatch, and the selected rank is thrown away because backward never runs.
- **Same waste elsewhere:** the no-grad first pass of full activation recompute also runs the selection, and so does any frontend that never calls `prepare_packed_seq_params`.

**Expected:** only select the HCA backward when a backward can follow.

**Fix** (gate the selection on autograd being enabled):
```suggestion

```
`training_with_grad` (L3493) would also work, but it additionally sends eval-mode-with-grad forwards to the stock path. `torch.is_grad_enabled()` is the smallest condition that keeps the invariant.

**Must keep working**
- Training forwards with grad, both eager and during TE/local graph capture, still select HCA and still record the `_assert_async` boundary guard.
- The recompute forward inside backward runs with grad enabled, so full and selective recompute still use the HCA backward.
- The forward output is unchanged: FlashMLA forward is the same on both branches.
- `test_aligned_hca.py` and `test_dev_aligned_hca_backward_replays` call `aligned_hca_cp_rank`/`csa_sparse_attn` directly, so they are unaffected.

- Proposed test (not run): patch `csa.aligned_hca_cp_rank` with a `Mock` and run the THD-CP forward on an eligible layout.
  - Under `torch.no_grad()`: the mock is not called and `csa_sparse_attn` receives `hca_cp_rank=None`.
  - With grad enabled: the mock is called exactly once and its return value is passed through.
- Static invariant: the `aligned_hca_cp_rank` call is reachable only when `torch.is_grad_enabled()` is true.

**[SUGGESTION Memory]** When `hca_cp_rank` is set, the backward goes to `aligned_hca_backward`, which never reads `topk_idxs` or `topk_length`. Forward still saves `topk_idxs` ([L1945-L1947](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L1945-L1947)).

- **Why it costs memory:** in the THD-CP path without an indexer, nothing else holds `topk_idxs` after `_forward_thd_cp` returns. So this save alone keeps an `(l_local, 128 + max_seqlen_q // 128, aligned to 64)` int32 buffer alive until backward, for every HCA layer.
- **Size:** about 10.5 MB per layer at 64K/CP16, and about 151 MB per layer at 128K/CP4.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

## Strict review: opt-in aligned HCA backward (#7625)

**Findings:** CRITICAL 0, IMPORTANT 1, SUGGESTION 3. **Overall risk: low.**

The flag is off by default and eligibility is checked conservatively. With the flag off, or on an ineligible layout, the stock backward runs unchanged. I found no correctness defect that could produce wrong gradients.

### Most important finding
- **[IMPORTANT Performance]** ([csa.py L3993](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L3993)): HCA selection also runs in forward passes that never reach backward.
  - Setup: Transformer Engine (TE) CUDA graphs that capture attention. In that setup [`prepare_packed_seq_params`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/training/utils/packed_seq_utils.py#L32) skips the per-microbatch preparation. Evaluation then runs eagerly, because TE graphs require `self.training` ([module.py L812-L822](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/module.py#L812-L822)).
  - Result: every HCA layer falls back to the live `.item()` in [`_is_single_sequence`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/aligned_hca.py#L61). That is the per-layer sync the review follow-up removed from eager training, and the result is never used because backward does not run.
  - Fix: one line — select only when `torch.is_grad_enabled()`.

### Suggestions
- **`hca_cp_size` defaults to 16.** This appears in three signatures, and the parameter is missing from the docstring. A future caller that passes only `hca_cp_rank` would silently get the CP16 layout ([fused_sparse_attention.py L2026](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L2026)).
- **`topk_idxs` is still saved for backward when the HCA backward is used**, even though that backward never reads it ([fused_sparse_attention.py L1953](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L1953)).
- **The new determinism-manifest note is incomplete.** It doesn't name the external kernel or explain how determinism is achieved. It also doesn't say that its replay test skips on the H100 kernel bucket ([manifest.py L135](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py#L135)).

### Checked, no issues found
- **Selection rule vs. the real `_forward_thd_cp` key/value (KV) layout.**
  - For ratio 128, the compressor capacity per rank is `c_cap = (l_local + 128) // 128` with alignment 1 ([thd_layout_kernels.py L1123-L1126](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/thd_layout_kernels.py#L1123-L1126)). With 128-aligned chunks that equals `l_local // 128 + 1`, so the `kv` shape check matches `cat(boundary, local, rank-major compressed)`.
  - The path without an indexer builds its attention indices from the padded `cu_seqlens` (`cu_seqlens_unpadded=None`). That matches the single-padded-sequence rule HCA assumes.
  - Window-only layers, indexer layers and the indexer-loss path never reach the HCA call.
- **Autograd.**
  - There are 13 forward inputs and 13 gradients are returned.
  - The new parameters come last and have defaults, so existing positional callers are unaffected.
  - When `kv` is rebuilt from its saved parts for backward, and when output RoPE is undone, the HCA branch sees the same tensors as the stock branch.
- **Prepared-verdict safety.**
  - The cached verdict is keyed on the `cu` tensor's identity, `cu._version` and the sequence length, and it is refreshed every microbatch.
  - `finalize_packed_seq_params` mutates the object in place.
  - `max_seqlen_q` is a Python `int` in the training pipelines, so the `!=` comparison stays on the host.
  - Moving the `cuda_graph_captures_attention` import to module level adds no import cycle: `transformer_config` already imports `cuda_graph_config`.
  - Configs without the flag short-circuit, so behaviour is unchanged.
- **Earlier reviewer feedback ([ghadiaravi13](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7625), comments on an older commit).** Both points are addressed in the current code:
  - `supports_configuration` now runs before the capture-time `_assert_async` ([aligned_hca.py L106-L115](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/036041092fb0eebbee741d6b5e2fa845e7a06036/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/aligned_hca.py#L106-L115)).
  - The per-layer `.item()` is replaced by the per-microbatch prepared verdict in eager training. The finding above covers the remaining eval path.
- **Config, CLI, tests.**
  - `--hca-aligned-backward` is generated automatically from `TransformerConfig`.
  - The hybrid-MoE config snapshot is updated.
  - `kind="dispatch"` is a valid manifest kind, and the registered source changes together with its replay test.
  - Each fallback-test case trips the check it targets.
- **Fatal device assert under graph replay when pack boundaries change.** This is documented in the config docstring ("Captured replay must preserve boundaries"), and because the backend choice is fixed when the graph is captured, there is no safe fallback during replay. I treat it as an intentional design choice.

### Limitations
- I could not inspect the external cuDNN Frontend `AlignedHCABackward` / `aligned_hca_backward_wrapper` (NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1198). Its numerics and the determinism claim rest on the PR's GPU parity and replay tests, which I did not run.
- I split the review into three areas and gave each to a delegated reviewer. The report for the dispatch/autograd area never reached me, so I inspected that area myself; the conclusions above are my own.
